biteOfDay: Bass on Table Rock are fully in fall mode, holding on long points, gravel flats dropping into 20–40 ft, and offshore structure. Walleye and crappie are working brush piles and points. On Taneycomo, stocked rainbows remain aggressive while brown trout activity continues to build with the cooling water. Marabou jigs, zebra midges, scuds, small streamers, and eggs produce well during lower flows.

tableRock.clarity: Gin-clear near dam; verify arms locally

taneycomo.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F). Verify at the bank.
taneycomo.generation: ~5,039 cfs at 11:00 CT (USACE live). Overnight ~20; afternoon peak ~5,039. Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

species.name: Bass
species.technique: Topwater at dawn; deep spoon, shakey head, deep crank mid-day

species.name: Walleye
species.technique: Crankbaits, live bait (carried mid-summer pattern — not freshly guide-verified 07-21)

species.name: Crappie
species.depth: Deep timber & brush piles (James River/Long Creek arms)
species.technique: Small white or yellow jigs under deep-water docks

species.name: Trout
species.technique: Low-flow morning window; pink worms/jigs/midges; drift when generation heavy (Trophy Area nightcrawlers)

species.name: Bluegill
species.technique: Worms, small poppers — great for kids (mid-summer pattern carry)

species.name: Catfish
species.depth: Indian Point & near dam, shallows after dark
species.technique: Stink bait, hot dogs, cut/frozen bait — evening/night

tip: Insider tip: During early low-flow windows on Taneycomo (always confirm the current SWPA schedule at 866-494-1993), drift or wade the seams and current breaks with light 2-lb test and a 1/16- to 1/8-oz marabou micro jig in black, sculpin, or olive (often with an orange head) or a #18-20 zebra midge  Deadline-guard carry from 2026-11-13.
